WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Acts 7:2 "And he said"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:2 "And he said" Stephen's defense is very similar to the theology of the book of Hebrews. He answered the charges in two ways:

  1. the Jewish people had continually rejected Moses in the past
  2. the temple was only one of several ways that God used to speak with Israel

This is a direct answer to the charges brought against him in Acts 6:13.

▣ "Hear me" This is the AORIST ACTIVE IMPERATIVE form of the Greek word akouō. It is used in the Septuagint to translate the famous prayer of Judaism, the Shema (cf. Deut. 6:4-5). It is also used in the prophets to reflect the sense of "hear so as to respond" (cf. Micah 1:2; 6:1). It is difficult to be certain this technical connotation is present when these Jewish men express their Hebrew thoughts in Koine Greek words, but in some contexts like this it may be true.

Remember, these early Jewish believers were Hebrew thinkers communicating in Koine Greek.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHEMA

▣ "brethren and fathers" Stephen is acknowledging the presence of other Jewish leaders by the term "brothers" and members of the Sanhedrin (called "the Council") called "Fathers."

▣ "'The God of glory" This God of glory (cf. Ps. 29:3) appeared to the Patriarch Abraham (cf. Gen. 12:1, 15:1,4; 17:1; 18:1, 22:1), thus beginning the Jewish people.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GLORY (kabod, OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHEKINAH

▣ "Abraham" Abraham was considered the father of the Jewish people. He was the first Patriarch. His call and subsequent walk with God are described in Gen. 12:1-25:11. In Galatians 3 and later Romans 4 Paul uses him as the paradigm of justification by grace through faith.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

▣ "when he was in Mesopotamia before he lived in Haran" Genesis 11:31 implies that Abraham was in the city of Haran when YHWH spoke to him. However, the time of God's contact with Abraham was not specifically stated. Abraham was from the city of Ur of the Chaldeans (cf. Gen. 11:28,31), but later moved to Haran (cf. Gen. 11:31,32; 29:4) following God's command. The theological point is that God spoke to Abraham outside of the land of Canaan. Abraham did not own or possess any part of the Holy Land (cf. Acts 7:5) during his lifetime (except a cave to bury his family, cf. Gen. 23:9).

The term "Mesopotamia" (lit. "between the rivers") can refer to the different ethnic groups:

  1. a people group in the northern area of the Tigris and Euphrates (i.e., "Syria between the Rivers")
  2. a people group near the mouth of the Tigris and Euphrates (old Babylon)

entries.title: Acts 7:3 "Leave your country and your relatives, and come into the land that I will show you"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:3 "Leave your country and your relatives, and come into the land that I will show you" This is a quote from Gen. 12:1. The theological issue involved in this quote is when God says this to Abram:

  1. while he was in Ur before he took his father Terah and nephew Lot to Haran
  2. while he was in Haran and he waited until his father died to follow God south to Canaan

entries.title: Acts 7:4 "he left the land of the Chaldeans"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:4 "he left the land of the Chaldeans" Chaldea (BDB 505) may be the name of a district close to the mouth of the Tigris and Euphrates Rivers (see note at Acts 7:2). It later came to refer to the nation which developed in this region, also known as Babylon (BDB 93). This nation also produced many scholars who developed mathematical formulas related to the movement of the night lights (i.e., planets, stars, comets, etc.). This group of wise men (i.e., astrologers) was also known by the name Chaldean (cf. Dan. 2:2; 4:7; 5:7-11).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHALDEANS

▣ "Haran" Haran (BDB 357) is a city to which Terah, Abraham, and Lot moved (cf. Gen. 11:31-32). Another of Abram's brothers settled there and the place is called by his name (i.e., city of Nahor, cf. Gen. 24:10; 27:43). This city on the upper part of the Euphrates (i.e., tributary river, Balikh) was started in the third millennium B.C. and has retained its name until today. Just as a note of interest, Abraham's brother, Haran (BDB 248), is not spelled the same in Hebrew as the city.

▣ "after his father died" Many have seen a contradiction here between Gen. 11:26,32 and 12:4. There are at least two possible solutions.

  1. Abraham might not have been the oldest son, but the most famous son (i.e., listed first).
  2. The Samaritan Pentateuch has Terah's age at death at 145, not 205, as the Hebrew text.

See Gleason L. Archer, Encyclopedia of Bible Difficulties, p. 378.

entries.title: Acts 7:5 "He promised that He would give it to him as a possession, and to his descendants after him"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:5 "He promised that He would give it to him as a possession, and to his descendants after him" This is an allusion to Gen. 12:7 or 17:8. The theological key is not only God's promise, but Abraham's faith in God giving him a descendant as well as a land. This faith is highlighted in Gen. 15:6 (cf. Gal. 3:6; Romans 4:3).

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

entries.title: Acts 7:6
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:6 This predictive prophecy states Israel will be enslaved 400 years in Gen. 15:13,14. However, Exod. 12:40 has "430 years" instead of "400 years." The Septuagint (LXX) translates Exod. 12:40 as "and the sojourning of the children of Israel, while they sojourned in the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan was 430 years."

  1. The rabbis have said that the number "400 years" starts with the offering of Isaac in Genesis 22.
  2. John Calvin has called the 400 years a round number.
  3. It may relate to four generations of 100 years each (cf. Gen. 15:16).

entries.title: Acts 7:7 "And whatever nation"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:7 "And whatever nation" This is a quote from the Septuagint of Gen. 15:14. This is not meant to be obtuse, but is a general statement. The nation was obviously Egypt. Other nations, however (i.e., Philistia, Syria, Assyria, Babylon), would become Israel's oppressors and God will judge them also.

▣ "and after that" This full phrase is a quote from Exod. 3:12. Stephen is reciting a loose, running history of Israel.

This text asserts that Canaan and Jerusalem will uniquely become YHWH's special place. This fits the emphasis of Deuteronomy (i.e., "to a land that I will show you").

▣ "in this place" In the context of the quote from Exod. 3:12, this refers to Mt. Sinai, which is also outside the Promised Land and is the site of one of the major events in the life of Israel (the giving of the Law to Moses, cf. Exodus 19-20).

SPECIAL TOPIC: LOCATION OF MOUNT SINAI

entries.title: Acts 7:8 "covenant"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:8 "covenant" See SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

▣ "circumcision" This was practiced by all of Israel's neighbors, except the Philistines (Greek Aegean people). For most cultures it was usually a rite of passage into manhood, but not for Israel, where it was an initiation rite into the covenant People. It was a sign of a special faith relationship with YHWH (cf. Gen. 17:9-14). Each Patriarch circumcised his own sons (i.e., acted as priest for his own family). Robert Girdlestone, Synonyms of the Old Testament, p. 214, says the rite of circumcision connected the rite of blood-shedding with the act of circumcision. Blood was connected to

  1. covenant forming rites (cf. Gen. 15:17)
  2. covenant breaking (cf. Gen. 2:17)
  3. covenant redemption (cf. Isaiah 53)

▣ "the twelve patriarchs" This usually refers to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, but here it refers to Jacob's twelve sons, who will become the tribes of Israel.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

entries.title: Acts 7:9 "Joseph"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 7:9 "Joseph" This account is found in Gen. 37:11,28; 45:4. Stephen is trying to show that the Jewish people and their leaders have often rejected God's chosen leader (cf. Moses in Acts 7:35).

entries.title: Acts 7:10
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 7:10 This account is found in Gen. 39:21; 41:40-46; see notes online.

entries.title: Acts 7:11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 7:11 This account is found in Gen. 41:54-55; 42:5, see notes online.

entries.title: Acts 7:12
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 7:12 This account is found in Gen. 42:4; see notes online.

entries.title: Acts 7:13
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 7:13 This account is found in Gen. 45:1-4; see notes online.

entries.title: Acts 7:14 "seventy-five persons"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:14 "seventy-five persons" This follows the Septuagint (LXX) and the Dead Sea Scrolls (DSS; 4QExa) manuscripts, while the Masoretic Text (MT) has "seventy" (cf. Gen. 46:27; Exod. 1:5; Deut. 10:22). At first this seems like a manuscript problem between the LXX, which Stephen quotes, and the Hebrew text of Exod. 1:5. On further reflection it may be two ways of counting all the descendants of Jacob. The problem arises between Gen. 46:26 and 27:

  1. the MT of verse 27 has two sons born to Joseph in Egypt, while the LXX has nine, which means that Ephraim and Manassah later had more children between them
  2. in the Hebrew text Jacob and his wife are counted, but Ephraim and Manasseh's extra children are not counted

In the Greek text (LXX) Jacob and his wife are not counted, but the extra children of Ephraim and Manasseh are counted. Both are accurate, but they add up the descendants in different ways at different times in Jacob's life. The Hebrew texts known as the Dead Sea Scrolls also have "seventy-five persons" in Gen. 46:27 and Exod. 1:5. Philo of Alexandia was familiar with both numbers.

We are all the benefactors of modern scholarship when it comes to difficult texts or number problems like this one. There is a new type of biblical resource available today which targets these difficult texts. I recommend:

  1. Hard Sayings of the Bible, IVP
  2. More Hard Sayings of the Bible, IVP
  3. Encyclopedia of Bible Difficulties by Gleason Archer
  4. Answers to Questions by F. F. Bruce
  5. The Lost World of Scripture, by John Walton and D. Brent Sandy

For a discussion of Acts 7:14-15 see #1 pp. 521-522.

entries.title: Acts 7:15
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 7:15 This account is found in Gen. 46:5; 49:33; Exod. 1:6.

entries.title: Acts 7:16 "to Shechem"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:16 "to Shechem" There seems to be a discrepancy in Stephen's sermon from the Genesis accounts of

  1. the burial of Joseph recorded in Josh. 24:32
  2. the burial of Jacob recorded in Gen. 50:13

The problem is (1) the city; it should be Hebron, not Shechem, or (2) the patriarch; it should be Jacob, not Abraham. However, Abraham and Jacob both bought land (cf. Gen. 23:16; 33:19). At Hebron both Sarah and Abraham were buried (cf. Gen. 23:19; 25:9), as were Isaac and Rebekah (cf. Gen. 49:29-31) and Jacob (cf. Gen. 50:13). Although it is uncertain about a burial plot at Shechem, it is possible that Abraham had earlier purchased a field on his stop there in Gen. 12:6-7. Later Jacob redeemed that same piece of land (cf. Gen. 33:19; Josh. 24:32). This is obviously speculation, but Stephen appears to be very knowledgeable of the OT history and this would be the only way to reconcile the various accounts.

entries.title: Acts 7:17
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 7:17 This would refer to Gen. 15:12-16 (the Promise) and Exod. 1:7 (their large number).

entries.title: Acts 7:18 "until there arose another king"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:18 "until there arose another king" This is a quote from Exod. 1:8. There has been and continues to be debate among scholars on the date of the Exodus. The identity of this Egyptian king is caught up in the disagreement. One could identify him as an Egyptian king

  1. from the XVIII dynasty (1445 B.C.)
  2. from the XIX dynasty (1290 B.C.)
  3. to relate this Egyptian king to the first native Egyptian dynasty who overthrew the Hyksos (Semitic) rulers of Egypt. This would explain the use of heteros in Acts 7:18. A native Egyptian would not want Semites, like the Hebrews, in large numbers in his territory, fearing another invasion like the Hyksos.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE DATE OF THE EXODUS

entries.title: Acts 7:19
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 7:19 This account is found in Exod. 1:10ff; see notes online.

entries.title: Acts 7:20 "Moses was born"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:20 "Moses was born" This account is found in Exodus 2; see notes online.

▣ "was lovely in the sight of God" This is a Hebrew idiom of beauty (cf. Exod. 2:2). Even Josephus comments on Moses' beauty (cf. Antiq. 2.9.6). It must have been well known Jewish tradition.

entries.title: Acts 7:21
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:21 This account is found in Exod. 2:5-6,10; see notes online.

▣ "he had been set outside" This is the Greek term ektithēmi, which means "to expose" (cf. Acts 7:19) or "place outside." The Egyptians forced the Hebrews to abandon their male children to the elements and wild beasts so as to control their rapid population growth.

NASB, NKJV  "Pharaoh's daughter took him away"
NRSV, NJB, REB  "Pharaoh's daughter adopted him"
TEV  "the king's daughter adopted him"
Peshitta  "Pharaoh's daughter found him"

The term anaireō literally means "to lift up." Moses was literally "lifted up" out of the Nile River and by this act, became the adopted son of one of Pharaoh's daughters.

entries.title: Acts 7:22
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:22 Moses had the best academic and military training (so says Josephus) available in his day at the court of Pharaoh. Moses was a highly educated man.

▣ "he was a man of power in words and deeds" This must be a summary of Moses' later life because at his encounter with YHWH at the burning bush he claimed he could not speak well (cf. Exod. 4:10-17).

entries.title: Acts 7:23 "he was approaching the age of forty"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:23 "he was approaching the age of forty" I think it was D. L. Moody who said Moses' life can be divided into three groups of forty:

  1. for the first forty years he thought he was somebody (i.e., educated at Pharaoh's court)
  2. for the second forty years he thought he had become a nobody (i.e., exiled to the land of Midian because he killed an Egyptian, and learned the ways and terrain of the Sinai desert)
  3. for the third forty years he found out what God could do with a nobody (i.e., led the people of YHWH to the Promised Land)

SPECIAL TOPIC: SYMBOLIC NUMBERS IN SCRIPTURE, #7

entries.title: Acts 7:23-24
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 7:23-24 This account is in Exod. 2:11-12; see notes online.

entries.title: Acts 7:25
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 7:25 This verse is Stephen's assumptions (possibly Jewish traditions); it is not stated in Exodus. However, this is the theme of Stephen's message. God's people did not seek, know, or obey Him!

entries.title: Acts 7:26-29
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 7:26-29 This account is found in Exod. 2:13-14; see notes online.

entries.title: Acts 7:28
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:28 The question expects a "no" answer.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GREEK GRAMMATICAL TERMS

entries.title: Acts 7:29 "At this remark Moses fled"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:29 "At this remark Moses fled" This account is found in Exod. 2:15,22. Moses' fear at killing an Egyptian shows that Pharaoh was not supportive of his being an adopted child of one of his daughters. Even so, Hebrews 11:27 is clear!

▣ "and became an alien in the land of Midian" God appeared to Moses at the burning bush in the land of Midian (cf. Exodus 3-4) and revealed His law to him at Sinai in the land of Midian (cf. Exodus 19-20), which shows that God was not limited as to where He revealed Himself. This same emphasis on God revealing Himself apart from the temple in Jerusalem is seen in Acts 7:36, 44, 48, and 53.

▣ "became the father of two sons" This account is found in Exod. 2:22; 4:20; 18:3-4; see notes online.

entries.title: Acts 7:30
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:30 This account is found in Exodus, chapters 3 and 4.

▣ "an angel" In the OT text this angel is really YHWH. See full note at Acts 5:19. Notice how this angel is characterized.

  1. Exod. 3:2, "the angel of the Lord appeared to him in a blazing fire"
  2. Exod. 3:4, "when the Lord (i.e., YHWH) saw that he turned aside to look"
  3. Exod. 3:4, "God (i.e., Elohim) called to him from the midst of the bush"

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C. and D.

SPECIAL TOPIC: The Angel of the Lord

▣ "Mount Sinai" See SPECIAL TOPIC: THE LOCATION OF MT. SINAI

entries.title: Acts 7:32
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:32 This account is found in Exod. 3:6; see notes online.

▣ "fathers" In both the Hebrew text and Greek translation (i.e., Septuagint) the word is SINGULAR. In every other occurrence of the phrase it is PLURAL. The implication is that God knew Moses' slave father.

entries.title: Acts 7:33
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:33 This account is found in Exod. 3:5. Moses approached the bush out of curiosity, not religious devotion.

The exact reason for taking off his shoes is uncertain.

  1. shoes might be polluted (i.e., animal dung)
  2. taking off shoes might be a sign of intimacy or familiarity (i.e., at home)
  3. a cultural practice of the Patriarchs or Egyptian ritual

entries.title: Acts 7:34
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 7:34 This account is found in Exod. 3:7. For me this verse is so theologically significant for this reason: YHWH heard their prayers, saw the affliction, and responded. He came down to rescue them, but notice His rescue was effected through human instrumentality. God sent a reluctant Moses. God has chosen to deal with humans through humans!

entries.title: Acts 7:35 "This Moses whom they disowned"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:35 "This Moses whom they disowned" God's people regularly reject God's spokesperson (cf. Acts 7:51-52). This may even be the purpose of Acts 7:27!

▣ "with the help of the angel who appeared to him in the thorn bush" Again God came to an Israelite outside the Promised Land. God's activity was not limited to any locality. Much of Israel's history occurred outside Canaan and before the temple in Jerusalem. All through the Israelites' history God's leaders were rejected by their peers (cf. Acts 7:9,27-28,35,39). This is a recurrent theme.

This angel is depicted as deity (cf. Exod. 3:2,4). This divine physical manifestation can also be seen in Gen. 16:7-13; 22:11-15; 31:11,13; 48:15-16; Exod. 13:21; 14:19; Jdgs. 2:1; 6:22-23; 13:3-22; Zech. 3:1-2. However, it must be stated that "the angel of the Lord" is not always a divine physical manifestation; sometimes he is just an angel, a messenger, (cf. Gen. 24:7,40; Exod. 23:20-23; 32:34; Num. 22:22; Judg. 5:23; 2 Sam. 24:16; 1 Chr. 21:15ff; Zech. 1:11; 12-13).

SPECIAL TOPIC: The Angel of the Lord

entries.title: Acts 7:36
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 7:36 This is a summary of God's miraculous power (i.e., Moses' staff) through Moses and Aaron. Israel's rejection of Moses parallels their rejection of Jesus, even in the presence of signs and wonders!

entries.title: Acts 7:37-38
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 7:37-38 This is a Messianic quote from Deut. 18:15 (cf. Acts 3:22, where Peter quotes the same prophecy). Stephen is identifying God's presence during the Exodus and Wilderness Wandering Period as both God's angel and God's special successor of Moses (i.e., the Messiah, the Prophet). Stephen is not depreciating Moses, but truly listening to Moses!

entries.title: Acts 7:38 "congregation"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:38 "congregation" This is the Greek term ekklesia, but in this context, it is used in the sense of "the assembly of Israel," not church.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHURCH (ekklesia)

▣ "the angel who was speaking to him on Mount Sinai" Rabbinical theology asserted that angels were mediators between YHWH and the giving of the Law (see note at Acts 7:53). It is also possible that the angel refers to YHWH Himself (cf. Exod. 3:21 compared to 14:19; and also Exod. 32:34; Num. 20:16; Jdgs. 2:1).

SPECIAL TOPIC: The Angel of the Lord

SPECIAL TOPIC: LOCATION OF MT. SINAI

entries.title: Acts 7:39 "our fathers were unwilling to be obedient to him"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:39 "our fathers were unwilling to be obedient to him" Stephen is connecting the dots of OT rebellion. His implication is that the Jews have always rejected God's leaders, and now they have rejected the Messiah.

▣ "repudiated him" This account is found in Num. 14:3-4.

entries.title: Acts 7:40-41
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:40-41 This account is found in Exodus 32. This was not idolatry, but the creation of a physical image of YHWH, but was used in fertility worship (i.e., "rose up to play," Exod. 32:6,19).

M. R. Vincent, Word Studies in the New Testament, pp. 238-239, lists three possible Egyptian bull gods.

  1. at Memphis, a calf god named Apis, who was seen as an intermediary between humans and the gods of Egypt
  2. at Heliopolis, a bull god named Mnevis, also associated with fertility
  3. at Hermonthis, a bull god names Buchis was associated with a war deity, Mont

entries.title: Acts 7:41
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:41 Stephen interprets the golden calf as an idol (the temples at Dan and Bethel, cf. 1 Kgs. 12:26-30) and uses this historical event to introduce a quote from Amos 5, which implies that Israel, even as far back as the Exodus and Wilderness Wandering, was idolatrous and rebellious.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FERTILITY WORSHIP OF THE ANE

entries.title: Acts 7:42 "God turned away and delivered them up to serve"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:42 "God turned away and delivered them up to serve" Verses 42 and 43 are quotes from Amos 5:25-27 where Amos asserts that Israel was always offering sacrifices to foreign gods. It was a regular, and early, pattern of their history (cf. Josh. 24:20). This reminds one of the drastic statements of rejection in Romans 1:24,26,28.

▣ "the host of heaven" This refers to Sumerian, Assyrian, and Babylonian astral worship (cf. Deut. 4:19; 17:3; 2 Kgs. 17:16; 27:3; 2 Chr. 33:3,5; Jer. 8:2; 19:13).

There are several textual problems between the Hebrew text (MT) of Amos 5:25-27, the Greek text (LXX) and Stephen's quote:

  1. the name of the star god
    1. the MT has kywn or kaiwann, the Assyrian name for the planet Saturn
    2. the LXX has rypn or raiphan, which may be repa, the Egyptian name for the planetary god of Saturn
  2. the Hebrew text (MT) and the Greek text (LXX) have "beyond Damascus," while Stephen quotes "beyond Babylon"
     There is no known manuscript of Amos that has the reading. Stephen may have been combining the Assyrians exile, of which Amos speaks, with the later Babylonian exile of Judah, but substituting the place of exile.

The worship of astral deities began in Mesopotamia, but spread into Syria and Canaan (cf. Job 31:26,27). The archaeological discovery at Tell El-Amarna, which included hundreds of letters from Canaan to Egypt in the 14th century B. C. also uses these astral deities as place names.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD OF HOSTS

▣ "in the book of the prophets" This refers to the scroll that contained the twelve minor prophets (cf. Acts 13:40). The quote in Acts 7:42-43 is from the Septuagint of Amos 5:25-27; see notes online.

The next phrase in Acts 7:42 is a question that expects a "no" answer.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEBREW CANON

entries.title: Acts 7:43 "Moloch"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:43 "Moloch" The Hebrew CONSONANTS for the word "king" are mlk (BDB 574). There are several Canaanite gods whose names are a play on these three CONSONANTS, Milcom, Molech, or Moloch. Moloch was the chief fertility god of the Amorites to whom children were offered to ensure the health and prosperity of the community or nation (cf. Lev. 20:2-5; Deut. 12:31; 1 Kgs. 11:5,7,33; 2 Kgs. 23:10,13,14; Jer. 7:31; 32:35). A. T. Robertson, Word Pictures In the New Testament, vol. 3, p. 93, says Moloch was "an ox-headed image with arms outstretched in which children were placed and hollow underneath so that fire could burn underneath."

The mention of the term Molech in Lev. 18:21 in context of inappropriate sexual unions, has caused some scholars to assume that children were not sacrificed to Molech, but dedicated to him as temple prostitutes, male and female. The concept fits in the general practices of fertility worship.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MOLECH

▣ "the star of the god Rompha" This may be a Coptic name for the planet Saturn. The Egyptian Saturn was depicted as a bull head representing "Horus, the bull."

The other option is that it depicted the Roman god Osiris. But it must be admitted there is much confusion in trying to understand and identify Egyptian deities!

▣ "images" See SPECIAL TOPIC: FORM (tupos)

entries.title: Acts 7:44
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:44 This account is found in Exodus, chapters 25-31; 36-40; see notes online. These detailed plans of the tabernacle were revealed to Moses on Mt. Sinai. The NT book of Hebrews talks about a heavenly tabernacle or sanctuary (cf. Acts 8:5-6; 9:11,23) of which the earthly one was a copy. As Stephen dealt previously in this chapter with the charge of chapter 6 that he was against Moses (cf. Acts 6:11), now he begins to deal with the second charge that he was against the temple (cf. Acts 6:13).

SPECIAL TOPIC: TABERNACLE OF THE WILDERNESS

▣ "the pattern" See SPECIAL TOPIC: FORM (tupos)

entries.title: Acts 7:45
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:45 This covers a period of time from the conquest (either 1400 or 1250 B.C.) to the time of David (± 1011 B.C) to

  1. 971/70 B.C., Harrison
  2. 973 B.C., Young
  3. 961 B.C., Bright

entries.title: Acts 7:46
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:46 This reflects 2 Samuel 7, which is such a significant passage. It is the divine establishment of the Davidic kingship (also note 1 Chronicles 17).

There is a MSS variant in this verse.

  1. "house of Jacob" in P74, א*, B, D, H
  2. "God of Jacob" in אi2, A, C, E and the LXX of Ps. 132:5

Either way, it refers to the descendants of Abraham and the Patriarchs. See full technical note in Bruce Metzger's A Textual Commentary on the Greek New Testament, pp. 351-353.

entries.title: Acts 7:47 "Solomon who built a house for Him"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 7:47 "Solomon who built a house for Him" This account is found in 1 Kings 6-8 and 2 Chronicles 1-6.

entries.title: Acts 7:48
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:48 This statement is similar to Solomon's statement in 1 Kgs. 8:27 and 2 Chr. 6:18.

▣ "The Most High" Luke uses this title for YHWH in Luke 1:32,76; 6:35; 7:48; 16:17.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE MOST HIGH

entries.title: Acts 7:49-50
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:49-50 This quote is taken from the Septuagint of Isa. 66:1-2 (see notes online). The point is that even Solomon recognized that a building could not contain the God of creation!

Do these verses imply an argument for the inclusion of Gentiles? If so, it seems somewhat veiled. However, Solomon himself saw the temple as a place for the world to come to YHWH (cf. 1 Kgs. 8:41-43). It was the Greek-speaking Jews (i.e., the Seven in Acts 6) who saw and proclaimed the worldwide mission even before the Apostles recognized this aspect of Jesus' teachings (cf. Matt. 28:18-20; Luke 24:46-47; Acts 1:8). Stephen may have been asserting this by implication in Acts 7:50.

▣ "My feet. . .My hand" See SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN

entries.title: Acts 7:51 "You men"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:51 "You men" Stephen turns from the rebellion of Jewish leaders and people in the past to the current leaders and people in the temple hearing his message. They were and they are rebels against YHWH!

▣ "a stiff-necked" Stephens alludes to Moses' characterization of the children of Jacob/Israel (cf. Exod. 32:9; 33:3,5; 34:9; Deut. 9:6,13; 10:16; 31:27 [see notes online]).

▣ "uncircumcised in heart" This Hebrew idiom means unfaithful, disloyal, and untrustworthy (cf. Lev. 26:41; Jer. 9:25-26; Ezek. 44:7). This is the opposite of Deut. 10:16; Jer. 4:4!

▣ "and ears" This idiom refers to their unwillingness to hear and respond to God's messengers (cf. Jer. 6:10).

▣ "are always resisting the Holy Spirit" This is very similar to Isa. 63:10. God's love and faithfulness were extolled in Isa. 63:9,11-14, but the people's reaction was faithlessness (note Isa. 6:9-10)! This discussion clearly demonstrates mankind's ability to resist God! They have free choice!

SPECIAL TOPIC: PERSONHOOD OF THE SPIRIT

entries.title: Acts 7:51b-52
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 7:51b-52 This is the strong condemnation of the current Jewish leadership, just like the ancient Israelite leadership! The ancient people of God had killed God's messengers and now they have killed the Messiah. This is a recurrent theme (cf. Acts 3:14; 5:28).

entries.title: Acts 7:52 "Righteous One"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:52 "Righteous One" This is used as a title for Jesus in Acts 3:14 and 22:14. See fuller note at Acts 3:14.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HOLY ONE

SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

SPECIAL TOPIC: OT TITLES FOR THE SPECIAL COMING ONE

entries.title: Acts 7:53 "as ordained by angels"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:53 "as ordained by angels" This refers to the rabbinical interpretation of Deut. 33:2 from the Septuagint in which God gave the law to Moses through angelic mediation which seems to be confirmed by Gal. 3:19 and Heb. 2:2.

▣ "yet did not keep it" Stephen opened his defense with "hear" (BDB 1033) which may reflect the Hebrew Shema, "hear so as to heed" (cf. Deut. 6:4). Stephen and later James (Jesus' half brother) both assert "be doers of the word not merely hearers" (cf. James 1:22-23 following Jesus, Matt. 7:24-27; Luke 11:48; John 13:17; as did Paul, Rom. 2:13).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHEMA

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

entries.title: Acts 7:54 "they"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:54 "they" This PLURAL PRONOUN in context must refer to the members of the Sanhedrin (cf. Acts 6:15) and possibly others who attended the trial.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SANHEDRIN

NASB  "cut to the quick"
NKJV  "cut to the heart"
NRSV, Peshitta  "they became enraged"
TEV  "they became furious"
NJB  "they were infuriated"

This is an IMPERFECT PASSIVE INDICATIVE. It is literally "cut to the heart" (cf. Acts 5:33). Stephen's message really got to these leaders, but instead of repenting, they turned, as always, to rejection and murder (cf. Acts 5:33).

▣ "gnashing their teeth" This is an idiom for rage (cf. Job 16:9; Psalm 35:16; 37:12; Lam. 2:16).

entries.title: Acts 7:55 "Holy Spirit. . .God. . .Jesus"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:55 "Holy Spirit. . .God. . .Jesus" Notice the mention of the Triune God.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TRINITY

▣ "Being full of the Holy Spirit" The concept of being filled with the Spirit for proclamation of the gospel is unique to Acts (i.e., plēroō, cf. Acts 2:4; 4:8,31; plērēs, cf. Acts 6:3,5,8; 7:55; 11:24). See full note at Acts 5:17.

The biblical truths related to the Spirit are characterized as:

  1. the person of the Spirit (cf. John 14-16; see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PERSONHOOD OF THE SPIRIT)
  2. the baptism of the Spirit (cf. 1 Cor. 12:13; see SPECIAL TOPIC: BAPTISM OF THE SPIRIT)
  3. the fruit of the Spirit (cf. Gal. 5:22-23)
  4. the gifts of the Spirit (cf. 1 Corinthians 12; see SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT [gift of])
  5. the filling of the Spirit (cf. Eph. 5:18; see SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT (filling))

Of all of these, Acts focuses on #5. The early church leaders were empowered, apparently again and again, to boldly and powerfully proclaim the gospel of Jesus Christ. In Stephen's case the effectiveness of his sermon cost him his life.

▣ "gazed intently" Luke is very fond of this term (cf. Luke 4:20; 22:56; Acts 1:10; 3:4,12; 6:15; 7:55; 10:4; 11:6; 13:9; 14:9; 23:1). Stephen looked up, as was typical of the Jewish manner of prayer, but instead of a physical posture for praying, God allowed him to see into heaven itself.

▣ "saw the glory of God" Abraham saw this same "God of glory" in Acts 7:2. Notice that Stephen is not said to have seen God, but His glory. No one could see God and live (see full note online at Exod. 33:17-23). Job believed he would see God (cf. Job 19:25-27; Acts 7:55). Jesus promises that one day the pure in heart will see God (cf. Matt. 5:8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: GLORY (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: CAN HUMANS SEE GOD AND LIVE?

▣ "Jesus standing at the right hand of God" Jesus being at God's right hand is an anthropomorphic idiom for the place of divine power and authority (i.e., Acts 2:32-33; 3:21; 5:31; 13:33). The fact that Jesus was standing shows His interest and care for the first Christian martyr.

God revealed Himself to Stephen in the form and manner that Stephen could receive (i.e., a variation of Ps. 110:1). This does not mean to imply

  1. that heaven is "up"
  2. that God is sitting on a throne

It does mean to convey Jesus' care and concern. We must be careful of culturally conditioned anthropomorphic language as the source of doctrine. Modern western readers' trying to take every passage literally as a way to show trust or devotion to the Bible is an unfortunate cultural trend. God truly reveals Himself to His creation, but He does so in earthly ways and forms in which they can understand. There is surely an element of accommodation. Fallen, finite, human creatures are not able to fully comprehend the spiritual realm. God chooses things in our cultural and experiential world to use as analogies and imagery to communicate to us. These are surely true, but not exhaustive.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PROBLEMS AND LIMITATIONS OF HUMAN LANGUAGE

SPECIAL TOPIC: WAYS OF REVELATION

entries.title: Acts 7:56 "Son of Man"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:56 "Son of Man" Stephen obviously is identifying Jesus with the "Righteous One" of Acts 5:52. His hearers would not have missed this Messianic affirmation. The title "son of man" has two OT usages:

  1. it was a common phrase for a person (i.e., Ezek. 2:1; Ps. 8:4)
  2. it was used of the divine personage (i.e., Messiah) in Daniel 7:13-14; Ps. 110:1; Mark 13:26; 14:62

Therefore, based on Daniel 7, it had connotations of both humanity and deity. This is why Jesus used it as a self-designation and also because it was not used by the rabbis who tended to use OT titles in exclusivistic, nationalistic, and militaristic ways. This reference by Stephen is the only one to use this phrase outside of the words of Jesus (cf. John 12:34).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SON OF MAN

entries.title: Acts 7:57 "rushed at him with one impulse"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 7:57 "rushed at him with one impulse" This is the very term used so often by Luke to describe the unity of the early disciples (cf. Acts 1:14; 2:46; 5:12; 15:25). The Sanhedrin was unified in their anger and rejection of Stephen (also see Acts 18:12, where the Jews of Achaia reject Paul and Acts 19:29 of the anger of the pagans of Ephesus against Christians).

entries.title: Acts 7:57-58
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:57-58 These hearers believed that Stephen had blasphemed by asserting that Jesus was the coming Son of Man (cf. Dan. 7:13). For these monotheistic Jews this was just too much! They did to Stephen what Moses mandated for blasphemy (cf. Lev. 24:14-16; Deut. 13:9; 17:7). Stephen's affirmation is either true or he is a blasphemer worthy of death! There can be no middle ground about the claims of Jesus (cf. John 14:6-9).

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

entries.title: Acts 7:58 "driven him out of the city"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:58 "driven him out of the city" No one could be killed inside Jerusalem because it was "holy" ground!

▣ "stoning him" It is often stated that the Jews under Roman occupation did not have the right of capital punishment. This shows that that is not always true. Mob violence could not be stopped quickly.

SPECIAL TOPIC: STONE TO DEATH

▣ "a young man named Saul" In Jewish circles, one was considered young up to age 40. This is our first encounter with Saul of Tarsus by name, later to become Paul the Apostle. Paul heard Stephen's OT survey and possibly had heard him earlier in the synagogue of the Cilicians in Jerusalem (Acts 6:9). One wonders whether this began Saul's period of doubt, which he tried to deal with by persecuting Christians.

entries.title: Acts 7:59 "Lord Jesus, receive my spirit"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:59 "Lord Jesus, receive my spirit" This is an AORIST MIDDLE IMPERATIVE. Notice that Stephen believed that he was going to heaven to be with Jesus (cf. 2 Cor. 5:6,8) and not to hades (i.e., the holding place of the dead like the Hebrew sheol). Stephen may have witnessed Jesus' crucifixion, or at least had heard about it in detail because he uses two similar phrases (i.e., Acts 7:59 and 60, cf. Luke 23:34,46).

It is interesting to note that Stephen prays to Jesus, as did the disciples in Acts 1:24. However, in the rest of the NT prayer is made to the Father in the name of the Son.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHERE ARE THE DEAD?

SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT IN THE NT

SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT IN THE BIBLE

entries.title: Acts 7:60 "falling on his knees"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:60 "falling on his knees" Stoning was not always a quick experience. The text implies it took several minutes.

▣ "he cried out with a loud voice" This also mimics Jesus' experience. These words were as much for the crowd as for YHWH. These words must have echoed in Saul's ears.

▣ "he fell asleep" This is biblical imagery for physical death (ex. Job 3:13; 14:12; Ps. 76:5; 2 Sam. 7:12; 1 Kgs. 2:10; Jer. 51:39,57; Dan. 12:2; Matt. 27:52; John 11:11; Acts 7:60; 13:36; 1 Cor. 15:6,18,20; 1 Thess. 4:13; 2 Pet. 3:4). This does not affirm the doctrine of "soul-sleep."

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. What is the purpose of Stephen's statement?
    What did it show about the Jews?
    Why were they so enraged?
  2. How was Jesus like Moses, Acts 7:37?
  3. Why is the quote from Isaiah 66:1-2 in Acts 7:49-50 so important?
  4. What was so significant about Stephen's vision of Jesus?

entries.title: Acts 8:1 "Saul was in hearty agreement with putting him to death"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:1 "Saul was in hearty agreement with putting him to death" This phrase concludes Acts 7. It is a PERIPHRASTIC IMPERFECT ACTIVE. Paul remembered this experience with great shame (cf. Acts 22:20; 1 Cor. 15:9; Gal. 1:13,23; Phil. 3:6; 1 Tim. 1:13). Some relate this passage to Acts 26:10, where it is assumed Paul voted in the Sanhedrin to put Christians to death.

▣ "on that day a great persecution began against the church in Jerusalem" This probably represents the activity of the Jewish leaders (mostly Sadducees) because of the exploding growth (even among priests) and prominence of the early church in Jerusalem. However, it was also God's way of forcing the church to implement Acts 1:8! If not 1:8 then 8:1!

It is not by accident that Luke uses the term ekklēsia for the new body of believers. These men and women did not see themselves as something separate from God's OT promises, but the fulfillment! The term was used in the Septuagint to translate "the congregation (MT ‒ qahal) in the wilderness" (cf. Acts 7:38); now it is used of the fellowship of believers in Jerusalem.

Luke is very fond of the term "great" (megas). He uses it twenty-five times in his Gospel and twenty-nine times in Acts. In Acts 8 he uses it for:

  1. great persecution, Acts 8:1
  2. great lamentation, Acts 8:2
  3. loud voice, Acts 8:7
  4. someone great, Acts 8:9
  5. to the greatest, Acts 8:10
  6. great miracles, Acts 8:13

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHURCH (ekklēsia)

▣ "they were all scattered throughout the region. . .except the apostles" It is extremely interesting that the persecution bypassed the Apostles and landed squarely on the Hellenistic Jewish Christians. Apparently at this stage the Apostles were still content to remain within Judaism. This event occurred some time after their meeting with Jesus in Galilee (cf. Matt. 28:18-20) and the Pentecost experience (esp. Acts 1:8). Still the Apostolic leadership was content to remain and preach only to Jews or proselytes and only in the Jerusalem area.

▣ "scattered throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria" This is in fulfillment of Luke's Great Commission mentioned in Acts 1:8. It has been some time now since Jesus spoke these words but apparently persecution was the only means of getting the church to go into all the world. The church is still reluctant!

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Acts 8:2 "Some devout men buried Stephen"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:2 "Some devout men buried Stephen" The term "devout men" is usually used of spiritually sensitive Jews (i.e., Simeon, cf. Luke 2:25). It is possible that this refers to

  1. Jewish Christians
  2. or simply Jews who disagreed with the illegal procedures (i.e., mob violence) and execution of Stephen

The Mishnah permits the burial of blasphemers, but not with the loud lamentations made by those who bury them. These devout men grieved openly

  1. in defiance of what happened
  2. in reference to the fact that what happened was not officially sanctioned

entries.title: Acts 8:3 "Saul began ravaging the church"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:3 "Saul began ravaging the church" This VERB is an IMPERFECT MIDDLE INDICATIVE. This can mean

  1. the beginning of an action in past time (cf. NASB, NJB)
  2. recurrent action (cf. NKJV, NRSV, TEV)

The term "ravage" meant "the tearing of a body by an animal." It is used in the Septuagint of

  1. animals in Exod. 22:13; Ps. 74:13
  2. military defeat in Jer. 28:2 and 31:18

Paul apparently was struggling with the truth of Stephen's statements, and may have tried to cover up his internal tension by aggressively persecuting the church (cf. Acts 9:1,13,21; 22:4,19: 26:10-11; 1 Cor. 15:9; Gal. 1:13; Phil. 3:6; 1 Tim. 1:13).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHURCH (ekklēsia)

▣ "entering house by house" This phrase could be understood in two ways:

  1. Paul found out where the Apostles had visited (cf. Acts 5:42)
  2. there were several house churches even at this early date in Jerusalem where believers met regularly

The early Christians would meet at

  1. the local synagogues every Sabbath
  2. the temple on special days or even most days
  3. numerous homes on Sundays
  4. special locations like the ones recorded in 1 Corinthians 11

▣ "dragging off men and women" This is a VERB that is used for Satan sweeping a third of the stars from heaven in Rev. 12:4. It is used several times in Acts (cf. Acts 8:3; 14:19; 17:6). Saul was vicious in his persecution (cf. Acts 26:10). This is evidenced by the phrase "men and women." He tore apart families of sincere believers and had them imprisoned and some even killed (cf. Acts 9:1,13,21; 22:4,19; 26:10,11; Gal. 1:13;23; 1 Tim. 1:13). This is why he later calls himself "the least of the saints" (cf. 1 Cor. 15:9; Eph. 3:8).

entries.title: Acts 8:4 "those who had been scattered went about preaching the word"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:4 "those who had been scattered went about preaching the word" Notice it was not the Apostles, because they remained in Jerusalem, but the Hellenistic Jewish Christians scattered throughout the region who became the early evangelists. It is amazing that the worldwide mission of the church was instigated, not by the Apostles, but by Stephen and Philip.

For "preaching" see SPECIAL TOPIC: KERYGMA OF THE EARLY CHURCH

The "word" here must surely mean the gospel, but also the added worldwide, non-Jewish focus of Stephen (Great Commission, Acts 1:8; Matt. 28:18-20; Luke 24:47).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE GOSPEL

entries.title: Acts 8:5 "Philip"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:5 "Philip" He is one of "the Seven" mentioned in Acts 6:5 (cf. Acts 21:8-9). He is depicted in three evangelistic settings: (1) Samaria; (2) the Ethiopian Eunuch; and (3) ministry in the Palestinian coastal area (i.e., Philistine area). These "seven" had a heart for evangelism.

▣ "went down to the city of Samaria" There is a manuscript question over whether the text reads "the city of Samaria" or "a city of Samaria" (Peshitta, REB, NJB). Manuscript attestation is slightly in favor of the DEFINITE ARTICLE (UBS4 gives it a "C" rating, cf. MSS, P74, א, A, B). However, this city was not known by the name Samaria at this time, but as Sebaste. During this Roman period the term Samaria was used of the whole district. The major city of Samaria would have been Shecham, then called Neapolis and today Nablus. It has been theorized that this city may be Gitta because that is the traditional home of Simon Magus. This theory is from Justin Martyr, who was also from this area. See F. F. Bruce, Answers to Questions, p. 77.

▣ "and began proclaiming Christ to them" The Samaritans were hated by the Jews because they considered them to be half-breeds (cf. Ezra 4:1-3). This was related to the Assyrian exile of 722 B.C. that repopulated the area of the northern Ten Tribes with pagans who intermarried with the small remaining Jewish population (cf. 2 Kings 17:24-41).

This group of people was also ministered to by Jesus. Jesus revealed His Messiahship to a woman of Samaria and her village (cf. John 4). Now Philip preaches about "the Christ" (DEFINITE ARTICLE), which is the Greek translation of "The Messiah." The OT title relates to YHWH's promise of sending One who would set up the new kingdom and inaugurate the New Age of the Spirit. This event is foreshadowed in Jesus' ministry and specifically mandated in Jesus' closing words (Acts 1:8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIAH

SPECIAL TOPIC: OT TITLES FOR THE SPECIAL COMING ONE

entries.title: Acts 8:6 "The crowds with one accord"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:6 "The crowds with one accord" The phrase "one accord" is very popular with Luke. See note at Acts 1:14.

▣ "as they heard and saw the signs which he was performing" This refers to miracles confirming Philip's message (cf. Acts 8:7). These same manifestations of the Spirit accompanied Jesus, the Twelve, the seventy, Peter, John, and Paul's preaching.

entries.title: Acts 8:7
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:7 Demon possession is a reality in our world (cf. Merrill F. Unger's two books: [1] Biblical Demonology and [2] Demons in the World Today). Jesus' power over the demonic was continued by His representatives (the Apostles, the seventy, the Seven, Paul). Satan's Kingdom has been vanquished!

SPECIAL TOPIC: DEMONS (unclean spirits)

SPECIAL TOPIC: EXORCISM

entries.title: Acts 8:9 "a man named Simon"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:9 "a man named Simon" Whether this man truly believed (cf. Acts 8:13,18) or was simply a charlatan seeking power is uncertain. I would like to give him the benefit of the doubt based on Acts 8:24. It is amazing how much tradition the early church developed around this man, but all of it is speculative (cf. The Zondervan Pictorial Encyclopedia of the Bible, vol. 5, pp. 442-444).

NASB, NRSV, Peshitta  "magic"
NKJV, TEV  "sorcery"
NJB, REB  "magic arts"

Magic was/is an attempt to control events by supernatural means. It involves the spiritual forces of the evil one.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MAGIC

entries.title: Acts 8:10 "This man is what is called the Great Power of God"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 8:10 "This man is what is called the Great Power of God" This was a title for the high god of the Greco-Roman Pantheon (i.e., Zeus). In Aramaic it would be "This is the power of the god who is called great." This man had thoroughly tricked the locals. He may have even tricked himself (cf. Acts 8:9,13).

entries.title: Acts 8:12 "believed"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:12 "believed" Notice "belief" is impossible without the Spirit. Salvation was real but the Spirit's empowerment would come later with the laying on of hands by Peter and John.

The term "believed" is used of a true faith encounter with Jesus, but also of a false faith encounter (i.e., John 8:31 vs. the rest of the chapter; Matt. 13:20-21). True faith

  1. has observable characteristics (John 8:39-44)
  2. moves through time until death (Matt. 24:13)
  3. is correct theology about the person of God, His Son, and how one is saved

SPECIAL TOPIC: FAITH, BELIEVE, OR TRUST

NASB  "preaching the good news"
NKJV, Peshitta  "preached the things"
NRSV  "was proclaiming the good news"
TEV  "message about the good news"

This is the Greek VERB euangelizō, which is a compound of good (eu) and message (angelizō). We get the English words evangel, evangelize, and evangelism from this Greek term. It is first used in Mark 1:1 and is translated "the gospel." Philip presented the story of Jesus to these Samaritans and they responded in saving faith.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE GOSPEL

▣ "about the kingdom of God" Jesus spoke often of the Kingdom of God in the Synoptic Gospels. This emphasis continues in Acts (cf. Acts 1:3; 8:12; 14:22; 19:8; 28:23,31). It is both present and future. See the Special Topic below for more details.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE KINGDOM OF GOD

▣ "the name of Jesus Christ" The power was from Jesus, not any other source.

SPECIAL TOPIC: The Name of the Lord (NT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: Christ Jesus As Lord

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIAH

▣ "they were being baptized" See SPECIAL TOPIC: BAPTISM

▣ "men and women alike" Contextually there may be two significances to this phrase.

  1. Paul persecuted "men and women (cf. Acts 8:3)," but the gospel also was saving "men and women"
  2. In Judaism only men participated in the initial Jewish rite of circumcision, but now in the gospel, both genders participated in the initial rite of baptism

SPECIAL TOPIC: WOMEN IN THE BIBLE

entries.title: Acts 8:13 "Simon believed"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:13 "Simon believed" Most evangelicals use this term "believed" in a very definitive sense, but there are places in the NT (e.g., John 8:31) where it denotes something less than conversion (cf. John 8:59). See note at v. 12.

Initial faith is not the only criteria (cf. Matt. 13:1-9,10-23; 24:13). Continuance and obedience are also evidence of a true relationship with Christ.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FAITH, BELIEVE, OR TRUST

SPECIAL TOPIC: PERSEVERANCE

▣ "he continued on with Philip" This is a PERIPHRASTIC IMPERFECT. Notice the sequence.

  1. he heard, Acts 8:6-7,12
  2. he saw, Acts 8:6-7,13
  3. he believed, Acts 8:13
  4. he was baptized, Acts 8:13
  5. he went with Philip, Acts 8:13

All of these appear to be true marks of a believer.

entries.title: Acts 8:14 "when the apostles in Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent them Peter and John"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:14 "when the apostles in Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent them Peter and John" Ministry to the Samaritans was forbidden to the disciples during Jesus' lifetime (cf. Matt. 10:5). Apparently, the Apostles wanted to give their official sanction to this radical and unusual movement of the Holy Spirit among this traditionally hated racial group. This area was specifically mentioned in Acts 1:8. As was typical, Philip caught Jesus' implication of world-wide evangelization quicker than the Twelve.

Notice that believing in Jesus is parallel to "receiving the word of God." The word of God can stand for several things.

  1. God's total communication to human beings
  2. God's recorded communication to human beings (i.e., Scripture)
  3. God's Son (i.e., the Word, cf. John 1:1) who is the ultimate revelation of God (cf. Heb. 1:3)

Notice that Peter and John were sent. Peter was the acknowledged leader of the Apostolic group and John the one who earlier wanted to call down fire on the Samaritans (cf. Luke 9:54).

The theological emphasis on human free will is crucial (i.e., "receive").

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHAT DOES IT MEAN TO "RECEIVE," "BELIEVE," "CONFESS/PROFESS," "CALL UPON"?

SPECIAL TOPIC: RECEIVE

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

entries.title: Acts 8:15 "who came and prayed for them that they might receive the Holy Spirit"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:15 "who came and prayed for them that they might receive the Holy Spirit" There are tremendous problems trying to build a theology of salvation from Acts for the following reason: the order of events and the events themselves surrounding salvation differs from passage to passage. The Holy Spirit in this passage refers to a confirmation, like Pentecost, showing that God had accepted and saved these Samaritans. They could not have truly been saved in the first place (i.e., receive is PERFECT MIDDLE INDICATIVE) without the work of the Holy Spirit (cf. Rom. 8:9).

I think the experience of Pentecost set a pattern, which God reproduced in the experience of different racial and geographical people groups, to show and confirm to the believing Jewish church that God Himself had fully and completely accepted a new group. The Spirit's manifestation in Acts (i.e., Pentecost) is thereby theologically different from the Corinthian tongues (see notes at Acts 2:4).

This text cannot be used to demand a Corinthian-like experience to confirm salvation (cf. 1 Cor. 12:29-30, which is a series of questions which expect a "no" answer). Luke records what occurred, not what should occur every time. See Fee and Stuart, How To Read the Bible For All Its Worth, pp. 107-126.

For "receive" see SPECIAL TOPIC: RECEIVE

SPECIAL TOPIC: SPEAKING IN TONGUES

entries.title: Acts 8:16
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:16 This could be called the Samaritan Pentecost.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SPEAKING IN TONGUES

entries.title: Acts 8:16-17
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:16-17 This is different from the stated order of salvation events in Acts 2:38. The discrepancy is due to the specific action of the Holy Spirit:

  1. in Acts 2:38 in relation to salvation
  2. in Acts 8:16 in relation to a Pentecostal type of experience

The same "Holy Spirit event" of Acts 2 now occurred with Samaritans. This was not for their benefit alone, but mostly for the Jewish Christian community. It showed them that God had fully accepted the Samaritans! This is not meant to assert a two-step initial salvation experience.

Please notice that it was Peter and John who noticed the absence of the special manifestation of the Spirit that they had experienced at Pentecost to clearly demonstrate that God accepted the hated Samaritans. This is not to imply that the miraculous signs which accompanied Philip's preaching were not true manifestations of the Spirit (cf. Acts 8:13). Peter and John wanted a Samaritan Pentecost! This is so important because when Cornelius has the same experience (i.e., Acts 10), Peter knew that God had fully accepted a Roman military man and his family and friends! The gospel is for all people. This is the great truth which this experience reveals in Acts!

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Acts 8:17
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:17 This cannot be a proof-text for the necessity of laying on hands. This procedure, for this purpose, does not occur again in Acts. It does express the power and authority of the Apostles.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LAYING ON OF HANDS

entries.title: Acts 8:20
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:20 The theological question for us is the soteriological question for Simon. Was he saved or not? Peter's word can be taken as a curse or a warning. All new believers have weak and incorrect information about the gospel, but does Simon's denote an added element of egotism? Can people be saved with conflicting priorities in their lives (i.e., Matt. 13:1-23)?

▣ "the gift of God" Here the Spirit stands for all of God's work on behalf of sinful rebellious humanity (cf. Isa. 53; 55:1-2; Jer. 31:31-34; Ezek. 36:22-36; Luke 11:13; Acts 2:38).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT (gift of. . .)

entries.title: Acts 8:21 "You have no part or portion in this matter"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:21 "You have no part or portion in this matter" The first term "part" (i.e., meris) means a portion in common. It has a negative connotation here and in 2 Cor. 6:15.

The second term "portion" (i.e., klēros) is the OT word for "lot," which was the way they determined the will of God (i.e., Urim and Thummim). They were used to divide the Promised Land among the tribes (cf. Josh. 12-19). Therefore, it is used in the sense of inheritance.

This term came to be used in English for "clergy," but in the NT it refers to all believers. The NT knows nothing of a clergy‒laity dichotomy! All believers are called, gifted, full time servants of God (i.e., Eph. 4:11-12)

SPECIAL TOPIC: URIM and THUMMIM

▣ "your heart is not right before God" This may be an allusion to Ps. 78:37. The terms "right" and "just" and their various forms, come from a term for a river reed found in Mesopotamia. It was fifteen to twenty feet tall and straight. God took this word, which was used in construction (checking the horizontal straightness of walls), to describe His own ethical character. God is the standard, ruler, straight edge by which all humans are judged. In light of this, all fail the test (cf. Rom. 3:9-18,23).

SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

entries.title: Acts 8:22 "repent"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:22 "repent" This is an AORIST ACTIVE IMPERATIVE, which denotes urgency. Salvation is impossible without repentance. There must be "a turning from" and "a turning to." Believers turn from self and sin and turn to God and His Son in faith.

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (NT)

▣ "pray" This is an AORIST PASSIVE (deponent) IMPERATIVE. Talking to God is evidence of a personal relationship, as conviction, which leads to repentance, is evidence of the indwelling Spirit!

▣ "if" This is a FIRST CLASS CONDITIONAL SENTENCE which is assumed to be true for the author's literary purposes or from his perspective. In this sentence it denotes a contingency based on Simon's willingness to repent and pray for forgiveness. His mindset and actions are a serious deviation from normative Christianity.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GREEK GRAMMATICAL TERMS, VII

▣ "the intention of your heart" Sin begins in the thought life. The rabbis say that the mind is like a plowed garden ready for seed. What we allow in through our eyes and ears takes root. If we dwell on it, these thoughts become actions. This is why the NT asserts that we should "gird up the loins of our minds" (cf. 1 Pet. 1:13) or "renew your mind" (cf. Rom 12:2; Eph. 4:23).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEART

8:23
NASB, NRSV  "the gall of bitterness"
NKJV  "poisoned by bitterness"
TEV  "full of bitter envy"
NJB, Peshitta  "bitterness of gall"

The terms "gall" (cholē) and "bitterness" (pikros) both refer to

  1. a bitter spirit, usually associated with anger and apostasy (cf. Deut. 29:18; 32:28-33; Heb. 12:15)
  2. The NET Bible associates the idiom with jealousy related to Peter's ability to pass on the Spirit with his hands.
  3. Paul uses the term "bitter" several times in lists of things to avoid (cf. Rom. 3:14; Eph. 4:31).
NASB  "in bondage of iniquity"
NKJV, Peshitta  "bound by iniquity"
NRSV  "chains of wickedness"
TEV  "a prisoner of sin"
NJB, REB  "chains of sin"

This may be an allusion to the work of the Messiah (cf. Isa. 58:6). Jesus could free Simon from this evil bondage as he freed him from the penalty of sin. Sin has two aspects:

  1. death both physically and spiritually
  2. who is in control in the sinner's life (it can affect both the saved and the lost, cf. 1 Cor. 3:1-3)

Sin must be dealt with both in time and in eternity; its penalty and power must be dealt with, but only Christ and the Spirit can do it, but we as believers must allow Them to!

entries.title: Acts 8:24 "Pray to the Lord for me yourselves"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:24 "Pray to the Lord for me yourselves" This is an AORIST PASSIVE IMPERATIVE PLURAL, which may refer to the entire mission team. Simon repeats Peter's words from Acts 8:22. Peter's words have frightened him. I believe Simon is a believer, but a new, baby one.

SPECIAL TOPIC: INTERCESSORY PRAYER

entries.title: Acts 8:25 "solemnly testified"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:25 "solemnly testified" See note at Acts 2:40.

▣ "the word of the Lord" This phrase refers

  1. in the OT to YHWH's message (i.e., Gen. 15:1; Isa. 1:10; 40:8), which will never pass away
  2. in the NT to Jesus' word (i.e., Acts 11:16; 13:12)
  3. in Acts to the gospel about Jesus (i.e., Acts 8:25; 12:24; 13:48-49; 15:35,36; 16:32; 19:20,20; also note Paul's usage in 1 Thess. 1:8; 4:15; 2 Thess. 3:1; see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE GOSPEL
  4. there is a specialized use of Logos, referring to the person of the Messiah in John 1:1-14; Rev. 19:13

SPECIAL TOPIC: LOGOS (word)

▣ "and were preaching the gospel to many villages of the Samaritans" This shows the marked change of attitude on the part of the Apostles to the Samaritans.

It seems that "the word of the Lord" and "the gospel" are synonymous.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE GOSPEL

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE KERYGMA OF THE EARLY CHURCH

entries.title: Acts 8:26 "an angel of the Lord spoke to Philip"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:26 "an angel of the Lord spoke to Philip" Here "the angel of the Lord" and "the Holy Spirit" seem to be synonymous (cf. Acts 8:29). Angels communicating with believers is common in Acts (cf. Acts 8:26; 10:37; 11:13; 12:7-11; 27:23). See note at Acts 5:19.

SPECIAL TOPIC: The Angel of the Lord

▣ "Get up and go south" These are both IMPERATIVES. This could refer to one of two roads to Egypt. This message may have been audible because of its specificity. This is obviously a divinely prepared evangelistic encounter (like Paul's Damascus Road).

NASB, REB  "(This is a desert road)"
NKJV  "This is the desert"
NRSV  "(This is a wilderness road)"
TEV  "(This road is not used nowadays)"
NJB  "the desert road"
Peshitta  "by way of the desert"

If this is a comment by Luke, is Luke clarifying his source, or is this a comment from Luke's source (probably Philip, cf. Acts 21:8)? These questions cannot be answered with certainty. Inspiration covers Bible productions no matter how many separate persons are involved.

SPECIAL TOPIC: INSPIRATION

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE BIBLE (its uniqueness and inspiration)

entries.title: Acts 8:27 "a court official"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:27 "a court official" The term "official" is literally the term "eunuch." However, it is uncertain whether he was a physical eunuch or simply an official at court (derived meaning). In the OT, Potiphar is called a eunuch and yet he is married (cf. Gen. 39:1). In the OT, Deut. 23:1 forbids a eunuch from becoming a part of the Jewish community; however, in Isaiah 56:3-5, this ban is removed. This clearly shows the New Age of the Spirit has dawned. Whether this man was a god-fearer or a proselyte is simply uncertain, but probable. The descriptive phrase implies he was a high government official from Ethiopia.

▣ "Candace, queen of the Ethiopians" "Candace" is a title like "Hadad," "Pharaoh," or "Caesar." The reason the queen is mentioned is because the king in Ethiopia was considered to be a deity and, therefore, it was beneath him to deal with simple administrative or political affairs.

entries.title: Acts 8:28 "reading the prophet Isaiah"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 8:28 "reading the prophet Isaiah" Apparently this man had bought an expensive leather scroll of Isaiah, which would have been over 29 feet long (i.e., one found in the Dead Sea Scrolls). By the Spirit's direction, he had opened it to the Messianic passage of Isaiah 53:7-8 and was reading it.

entries.title: Acts 8:29 "the Spirit said to Philip, 'Go up and join this chariot'"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:29 "the Spirit said to Philip, 'Go up and join this chariot'" This is an AORIST PASSIVE IMPERATIVE. It literally meant "be glued." The Spirit is giving Philip every specific guidance.

SPECIAL TOPIC: PERSONHOOD OF THE SPIRIT

entries.title: Acts 8:30 "Philip ran up and heard him reading Isaiah the prophet"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:30 "Philip ran up and heard him reading Isaiah the prophet" Ancients all read aloud even when alone.

▣ "Do you understand what you are reading" What a great question! It is possible to read Scripture and not clearly see its intent. The Spirit is directing Philip to a "divine appointment" which will

  1. show the New Age has dawned
  2. give a powerful witness to another people group

See my Bible Interpretation Seminar online (first red box on home page).

entries.title: Acts 8:31
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:31 A. T. Robertson's Word Pictures in the New Testament comments on this verse, "This is a mixed condition, the conclusion coming first belongs to the fourth class. . .with 'an' and the optative but the condition. . .is of the first class. . .a common enough phenomenon in Koine" (p. 110).

This FIRST CLASS CONDITION, like Luke 19:40 uses ean instead of ei. The CONDITION is determined by the MOOD, not the construction (cf. Luke 19:40).

SPECIAL TOPIC: GREEK GRAMMATICAL TERMS

entries.title: Acts 8:32-33
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:32-33 This quote is from a Messianic passage from the Septuagint of Isa. 53:7-9. I am surprised that these verses are emphasized and not other Messianic verses in this OT context. However, Philip starts right where he was reading and explains the entire passage in light of the life, ministry, death, and resurrection of Jesus of Nazareth. The OT prophecy has been fulfilled and forgiveness through Christ is offered to everyone!

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE KERYGMA OF THE EARLY CHURCH

entries.title: Acts 8:35 "Philip opened his mouth"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:35 "Philip opened his mouth" This shows the centrality of the OT passage concerning "the Suffering Servant" to gospel proclamation. I believe Jesus, Himself, showed the early church how these ancient prophecies applied to Himself when He ate with the two on the road to Emmaus (cf. Luke 24:27).

SPECIAL TOPIC: A SUFFERING MESSIAH

SPECIAL TOPIC: OT TITLES FOR THE SPECIAL COMING ONE

entries.title: Acts 8:36 "Look! Water! What prevents me from being baptized"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:36 "Look! Water! What prevents me from being baptized" Philip's gospel message included baptism (cf. Matthew 3; 28:19; Acts 2:38; Rom. 6:1-11; Col. 2:12)! Notice he did not need approval from the Apostles in Jerusalem to baptize a convert. Baptism is not a denominational issue, but a kingdom issue. We must be careful of the denominational traditions that have so muddied the biblical waters as far as the expected procedures in our day!

Was the eunuch worried about being accepted?

  1. racial issue
  2. physical issue
  3. socio-economic issue
  4. catechism issue

All barriers are down in Jesus Christ (cf. Eph. 2:11-3:13). Whosoever will may come (cf. John 1:12; 3:16-17; Rom. 10:9-13; 1 Tim. 2:4; 4:10; Titus 2:11; 2 Pet. 3:9)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: BAPTISM

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Acts 8:37
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:37 This verse, which records the eunuch's confession, is not included in the ancient Greek papyri manuscripts P45 (Chester Beatty Papyri), P74 (Bodmer Papyri), or the ancient uncial Greek manuscripts א, A, B, or C. Neither is it present in some of the ancient translations, Vulgate, Syriac, Coptic, or Ethiopian. Verse 37 is not original to Acts. UBS4 gives its omission an "A" rating, meaning certain. It is not even included in the text of NASB (1970) edition, but is included in the 1995 update with brackets.

SPECIAL TOPIC: TEXTUAL CRITICISM

entries.title: Acts 8:38-39 "went down into the water. . .came up out of the water"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 8:38-39 "went down into the water. . .came up out of the water" This is not a proof-text for immersion. The context implies they walked into a body of water, not the method of the baptism. This is also true of Jesus' baptism by John (i.e., Matt. 3:16). Be careful of your preconceived biases!

entries.title: Acts 8:39 "the Spirit of the Lord"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:39 "the Spirit of the Lord" This is a good example of the ambiguity related to the title "Lord" (kurios; note Acts 2:47; 11:21; 13:11; 16:14). It can refer to YHWH (OT) or Jesus (NT).
SPECIAL TOPIC: Lord (adon and kurios)
SPECIAL TOPIC: The Name of the Lord (NT)

The NT authors asserted Jesus' Deity in four specific ways.

  1. OT titles for YHWH used for Jesus (i.e., Lord, Savior, etc.)
    SPECIAL TOPIC: OUR SAVIOR
  2. OT activities of YHWH performed by Jesus (i.e., your sins are forgiven, cf. Matt. 9:2; Mark 2:5; Luke 5:20)
  3. texts on Jesus' Deity and pre-existence (i.e., John 1:1-14,18; 20:28; Phil. 2:6; Titus 2:13; Heb. 1:8; 1 John 5:20)
  4. grammatical features
    1. parallel phrases with one PREPOSITION
    2. parallel phrases with one VERB

▣ "snatched Philip away" Whether this is a miraculous occurrence like Elijah's (cf. 1 Kgs. 18:12; 2 Kgs. 2:16) or Ezekiel's (cf. Ezek. 3:14; 8:3) or simply a reference to his immediate departure is uncertain. The Spirit was intimately involved in this conversion. Notice also that extensive follow-up and catechism apparently did not occur, but the convert had the scroll of Isaiah and the indwelling Spirit!

SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT IN THE NT

▣ "went on his way rejoicing" The Good News is always accompanied by rejoicing (cf. John 15:11; 16:24; 17:13; Acts 8:8; Rom. 5:3; 1 John 1:4). Ireaneus records the tradition that this eunuch became a gospel missionary to his own people. The Spirit Himself must have done the follow-up discipling!

entries.title: Acts 8:40
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:40 Philip continued (IMPERFECT MIDDLE INDICATIVE) his evangelistic ministry in the Philistine town of Ashdod (i.e., Azotus) on his way home to Caesarea by the sea. It is obvious that Philip understood the universal evangelistic implication of the Samaritans and the Ethiopians. The gospel included even Philistines!

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. Why did God allow persecution to come upon the early Church?
  2. Why was the gospel being preached to Samaritans so significantly?
  3. Was Simon a believer?
  4. Why did the Samaritans not receive the Holy Spirit when they believed?
  5. What type of persons does the eunuch represent?
  6. Why is verse 37 not in all Bibles?

entries.title: Acts 9:1 "Saul, still breathing threats and murder"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:1 "Saul, still breathing threats and murder" This is literally "snorting." In Acts 26:11, Paul says of himself, that he was furiously enraged at them. Apparently Paul even voted to have some Christians put to death (cf. Acts 8:1; 26:10).

▣ "the disciples of the Lord" This term means "learners." It only appears in the Gospels and Acts. This term is rapidly replaced by the term "saints." Notice the number of terms used in this chapter to describe the people of God:

  1. disciples, Acts 9:1,10,19,25,26,36,38 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: DISCIPLES)
  2. the Way, Acts 9:2 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY)
  3. saints, Acts 9:13,32,41 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: SAINTS)
  4. brothers, Acts 9:17

▣ "went to the high priest" This is obviously a reference to the Sanhedrin (cf. Acts 26:10). See note on Sanhedrin at Acts 4:5.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SANHEDRIN
